title: Notion Not Syncing Across Devices: How to Fix It
body_md:
![notion.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/notion-not-syncing-across-devices-how-to-fix-it/1.png)
*Screenshot of notion.com ([source](https://www.notion.com/help/reset-notion))*

**Before troubleshooting, protect unsynced work.** If the affected device has edits that do not appear anywhere else, copy important text to a separate local file and preserve screenshots or attachments where possible. Do not sign out, clear local storage, reset or reinstall until you have protected those edits. Cloud-saved pages and unsynced local changes are not the same thing.

Next, check the page in a browser or on another device using the same account and workspace. If the latest edits are present there, restart the affected app and work through the steps below. There is no guarantee that resetting a device preserves changes that never reached the server.

## Why This Happens

![notion.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/notion-not-syncing-across-devices-how-to-fix-it/2.png)
*Screenshot of notion.com ([source](https://www.notion.com/help/notion-error-messages))*

Notion is cloud-first. It's a cloud-based app, and as long as you're connected, content syncs automatically — each device holds a local copy, and sync breaks when that copy and the server stop talking. The usual culprits:

- **A stale local cache or session.** The app keeps showing the old version of a page even though the server already has the new one.
- **Edits made offline that never uploaded.** Offline changes stay on the device and push to the cloud when you reconnect — but only if the app actually gets back online and stays open long enough.
- **Network or workplace restrictions.** Corporate firewalls, secure web gateways, and VPNs can quietly block Notion's traffic. Notion's own guidance is to ask your IT team to allowlist Notion's domains and IP addresses in VPN or firewall settings, and it publishes an allowlist guide to hand them.
- **An unsupported or outdated platform.** Chromebooks and ChromeOS devices aren't supported; Notion says to use Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge, or an Android or iOS device. The published system requirements at the time of writing are macOS 13 or above, Windows 10 version 21H2 or above and iOS 17.0 or above — older iPhones and iPads including the iPhone 8 and iPad Mini 4 are listed as unsupported.
- **A Notion-side outage.** Check Notion's status page before you start pulling the app apart.
- **You're in the wrong workspace or account.** Sounds silly, but if your work laptop is logged into a personal account, nothing will "sync."

## Step-by-Step Fixes

![notion.com official page screenshot](https://afroditena.github.io/mattress-checklist-android/assets/img/notion-not-syncing-across-devices-how-to-fix-it/3.png)
*Screenshot of notion.com ([source](https://www.notion.com/help/guides/working-offline-in-notion-everything-you-need-to-know))*

Work down this list only after protecting any unsynced changes. Stop as soon as the page updates. If the affected device contains the only copy of important edits and you cannot back them up, stop and contact Notion support before destructive troubleshooting.

### 1. Force-quit and reopen (30 seconds)

Not just closing the window — quit the app entirely (Cmd+Q on Mac, close it from the tray on Windows, swipe it out of recent apps on mobile), then reopen. In a browser, reload the tab. On desktop, Notion's reset guide starts even gentler: View in your menu bar → Force reload.

### 2. Confirm it's not Notion's fault

Open the page on a second device or in a browser. If the newest version shows up there, the problem is local to one device. If it's stale everywhere, check Notion's status page before touching anything else.

### 3. Sign out and sign back in

This rebuilds your session and forces a fresh pull from the server. Only do this after confirming that recent changes reached the server or that you have separately saved them. Do not sign out of all devices at once.

### 4. Test in a different browser or incognito window

Notion's own troubleshooting list suggests accessing Notion from a different device or browser, or from an incognito tab. If incognito shows the current version, you've got a cache or extension problem — move to the next step.

### 5. Clear the cache properly (browser)

**Warning:** Clearing site data can remove local state. First protect any content that has not synced and confirm that the cloud version contains the changes you need.

Notion advises clearing local storage and cache in your browser, then quitting and restarting it. For a deeper clean, Notion's reset guide walks through it for Chrome and Edge: open Developer Tools (cmd + option + i on Mac, ctrl + shift + i on Windows), right-click the refresh button, and select Empty Cache and Hard Refresh. Then go to Application in Developer Tools, expand Cookies, right-click the Notion link and select Clear. On Safari, open the Safari menu → Preferences → Privacy → Manage Website Data, find Notion, and select Remove All.

### 6. Reset the desktop app

**Last resort:** Verify the latest content on another device first. If it is missing there, preserve a local copy before resetting, or ask support for help. Resetting logs you out of any active Notion accounts, so have your login details ready.

The in-app route comes first: Help in your menu bar → Troubleshooting → Reset & Erase All Local Data. If that doesn't do it, close Notion and delete the Notion folder — on Mac, Finder → Go → Go To Folder → /Users/<USERNAME>/Library/Application Support; on Windows, C:\Users\<USERNAME>\AppData\Roaming. If you get an error deleting it, make sure Notion is fully quit — not in the background or system tray — and that no Notion processes are left in Task Manager. On phones and tablets, delete the app and reinstall it. Notion also says to make sure you're on the latest version.

One caution: if you have edits you made offline that never uploaded, get that device online and let it sync *before* you reset or reinstall.

### 7. Check the network, then escalate

Switch off the VPN, or hop to a different Wi-Fi network or your phone's hotspot. If sync works on cellular but not on the office network, the fix belongs to IT — send them Notion's allowlist guidance. Still stuck? Notion support can use a HAR file recording to diagnose network-level problems, so recording one before you write in will save a round trip.

## How to Prevent It Next Time

- **Give the app a beat before closing your laptop.** Most "lost" edits are edits that never finished uploading.
- **Mark pages as available offline on every device you use.** Open the page, select ••• at the top, and toggle on Available offline. This doesn't work in a web browser — desktop and mobile apps only. Sub-pages don't come down with the parent, so mark each one you need.
- **Know the database limit.** When you download a database or a page containing one, only the first 50 rows of the first view download; grab any additional important rows after that. Make sure the first view is the one you actually use.
- **Audit what's actually saved.** On Plus, Business, and Enterprise plans Notion also auto-downloads recently visited and favorited pages; Settings → Offline shows which ones.
- **Do permission changes while you're online.** Sharing, permissions, forms, buttons, embeds and AI blocks all need the server.
- **Keep every device on the latest app version.** Sync bugs get patched; old builds keep them.

*Updated October 2026: this guide is assembled from Notion's published help documentation and support guidance, not from a controlled test of sync failures.*

## My Take

My read is that most "Notion isn't syncing" panic is really a backup problem wearing a sync costume. The dangerous moment isn't the stale page — it's the five minutes later when you start clearing caches and resetting local data on the one device that holds edits the server never saw. Do the non-destructive checks first, in order, and you'll almost never need step 6.

I think the 50-row offline cap is the detail most people get burned by, because it fails silently. Your project tracker opens offline, looks normal, and rows 51 onward simply aren't there. If you fly a lot or work on spotty Wi-Fi, build a small offline-only page with the handful of things you actually need, rather than trusting a big database to come along for the ride.

The fair point on the other side: Notion's cloud-first design is why real-time collaboration works as well as it does, and offline mode arriving late is a consequence of that, not laziness. An app that merges conflicting edits across a team is a genuinely harder problem than one that syncs a folder of files.

Still, if your work is the kind where a lost afternoon is a real cost, I'd stop treating Notion as your only copy. Export the pages that matter on a schedule, or keep drafts in a plain-text editor and paste them in. A page marked "Available offline" is a cached copy, not a backup.

I'm not an IT or security professional, so on the firewall and allowlist side, hand Notion's documentation to the people who run your network instead of trying to work around it yourself.
